datasheet.title: EX3200 Ethernet Switches datasheet (Juniper Networks, 1000216-013-EN, Nov 2011)

description: Juniper EX3200-48P - a fixed 1RU Gigabit Ethernet access switch with 48 10/100/1000BASE-T ports, all of them Power over Ethernet. The front carries the 48 jacks in two stacked rows, an LCD panel with Menu and Enter buttons, three chassis status lamps and a slot for an optional uplink module, which ships covered. The rear carries the management and console jacks, a USB port, a temperature shutdown lamp, an ESD point, the earthing terminal, a fan tray and one power supply slot holding a 930 W AC supply. Air moves side to rear.

gaps.wanted: A straight-on photograph of the rear. None is held, so the rear is read off the guide's line drawing and the supply and fan art follows the isometric drawings.

A straight-on colour photograph of the front. The datasheet's photographs are greyscale perspective views from above, so the vertical positions carry a 6 percent foreshortening, every front position is estimated and no PoE colouring can be read.
The plate with a screw at each end between the USB port and the fan tray in Figure 3, 138.6 to 198 mm across. No callout or text names it, so it is not drawn.
A flat drawing or photograph of the two side panels, which carry the bracket holes; the guide draws no side elevation.
The bracket positions of the front, centre and rear mounting and of the 2-in-recess brackets: no figure in the guide measures them, so no ear position or kit is listed.
A library component for an LCD display; the LCD panel is a decor rectangle until one exists.
The fan tray's power draw: neither the guide nor the datasheet states it.

attrs.redundancy-note: Hardware guide, EX3200 Cooling System: one fan tray with one fan; the system raises an alarm if the fan fails and shuts down if the chassis overheats. The guide claims no tolerance of a failed fan

grounding.description: the rear earthing terminal, two 10-32 screws for a two-hole lug (Table 33)

lcd-buttons.description: the LCD panel's Menu and Enter buttons

mgmt.mixed: how the switch is reached out of band - the RJ-45 management Ethernet port, the RJ-45 console port and the USB port on the rear

attrs.redundancy-note: Hardware guide, Power Supply in EX3200 Switches: "The power supply in EX3200 switches is not redundant"

rj45.description: The 48 built-in 10/100/1000BASE-T ports, all of them PoE ports. rel-pos carries the number printed on the faceplate; the upper jack of a column takes the even number

status-leds.description: the three chassis status lamps right of the LCD panel

temp-leds.description: the temperature shutdown lamp on the rear panel

name: ex3200-48p

airflow.note: Guide, Airflow Direction in the EX3200 Switch Chassis and Figure 15: the fan tray "provides side-to-rear chassis cooling"; the datasheet gives 23.5 cfm. The chassis airflow enumeration has no side-to-rear, so `side` is written, the nearest answer.

chassis.note: Guide Table 5: height 1.75 in (4.45 cm) = 44.45 mm; width 17.25 in (43.82 cm) = 438.2 mm, "19 in. (48.2 cm) with mounting brackets attached", so 438.2 is the body between the bracket flanges; depth 17 in (43.18 cm) with no supply, with the 320 W AC supply or with the 190 W DC supply, and 19.25 in (48.9 cm) with a 600 W or 930 W AC supply (they extend 2.25 in). This model ships with the 930 W supply (Table 3), so the modelled depth is 19.25 in = 489.0 mm; the bare chassis depth is in attrs. THE DATASHEET DISAGREES: it gives 17.41 x 1.72 x 16.43 in (44.21 x 4.32 x 41.73 cm) and 18.8 in (47.8 cm) with the 600 W or 930 W supply. They are different measures of the same chassis (the datasheet's width is the desktop width), and the hardware guide is the newer and the more specific document, so the guide's figures are used; the datasheet's are in attrs. 1RU.

colour.note: The datasheet photograph is greyscale and shows a black face: the blank face of the 24-port view reads 59 of 255 in luminance and the top strip 50. The face is drawn #3b3b3b, neutral. The jack shells are drawn as the EX4200 draws them, the LCD green and the supply and fan faces are estimated; no photograph of the rear is held and the guide's figures are uncoloured line art.

ears.note: NOT MODELLED. The datasheet ships a 19-inch rack mount kit with each switch, and orders the four-post rack mount kit (EX-4PST-RMK) and the wall mount kit (EX-WMK) separately. The guide's mounting topics give the post and recess options, and no figure dimensions the bracket positions, so no ear position is written and no rail kit is listed in chassis.kits. The kit part numbers are recorded here for the later dedupe.

front-ports.note: 48 jacks in two stacked rows, four blocks of six columns across the face (guide Figure 1). The block starts read 8.9, 95.6, 182.9 and 269.8 mm from the left edge in the guide's drawing; the jacks are placed on the registry's 13.97 mm ganged-jack pitch with the blocks 88.0 mm apart, as the EX4200 front does, which agrees with the drawing to 1.3 mm at the second block and 3 mm at the fourth. Row centres read 16.8 and 31.6 mm down. The top row is the same part turned 180 so that its keyway is up.

front-right.note: Read off the guide's Figure 1 and the datasheet photograph (the EX3200 module panel is the EX4200's): the raised right-hand module panel 362.5 to 438.2 mm; the LCD window 375.5 to 411.2 x 10.3 to 19.9 mm; the Menu button centre (420.7, 12.5) and the Enter button (420.7, 20.7), 6.1 mm across; the three chassis lamps at x 427.8, y 9.05, 12.85 and 16.75; a face screw each side at (366.5, 22.0) and (429.9, 22.0); the uplink slot 366.9 to 429.9 x 26.5 to 41.0 mm. The model plate (296.5 to 344.0 x 0.9 to 5.0 mm) carries "EX3200" centred at 304.5 and the PoE count centred at 334.3, where the photograph prints them; Figure 1 draws the model name at the left of the top strip, beside the Juniper mark, which the photograph does not show. The top strip also carries the Juniper logo at the left, 6.4 to 22.2 x 1.0 to 5.1 mm, reserved as a logo zone and not drawn.

fru-bays.note: One power supply bay and one fan tray bay, each seating the guide's FRU parts (Field-Replaceable Units in EX3200 Switches; the fan tray, uplink module and transceivers are hot-removable). The guide says the supply "is not redundant". Nothing is built into the chassis.

gate-1-front.note: The datasheet photographs of the 48-port switches (page 4) are perspective views from above and a little front-on, 6 percent shorter than orthographic down. The guide's Figure 1 (g020081) is a vector drawing of the 48-port front whose face is 1380 px wide at the resolution it was read and gives the four jack blocks, the module panel, LCD and lamps; they are read from it and from the photograph together. No figure dimensions the face, so every front position is estimated and carries the same positions the EX4200 photographs give, which this front matches.

gate-1-rear.note: Guide Figure 3 (g020052) is a vector rear view with the top face in perspective: the chassis outline is 1407 px across for 438.2 mm (3.211 px per mm) and its face is 137 px high for 44.45 mm, so it is 4 percent foreshortened vertically. Positions across are read at 3.211 px per mm and heights at 0.325 mm per px from the top edge of the face. Every rear position is good to about 2 mm. Figure 3 is shared by all EX3200 models.

interface-names.note: Not printed and not modelled. The guide's Table 4 names the built-in ports PIC 0 and the uplink module PIC 1 and its examples name the network ports ge-0/0/0 and up and the uplink module's ports ge-0/1/0 and up. No table gives the numbering rule for every model, so the names stay out of the file as a block and go here.

lamp-legends.note: drawing-vs-photo: guide Figures 2 and 8 print ALM, SYS and MST beside the three lamps, to their right. The photograph cannot resolve type of that size, so it neither confirms nor contradicts the drawing. The legends are drawn as the guide draws them. Table 6 says the MST lamp "is meaningful only on EX4200 switches"; the lamp is on the face and is drawn.

lcd.note: The LCD panel shows two lines of 16 characters (guide, LCD Panel in EX3200 Switches). It is drawn as a window; no library component exists for a display and none is added, so it is a decor rectangle and not a part. Its colour is the EX4200's: the EX3200 photograph is greyscale.

other-faces.note: No source draws the top, bottom or sides flat: the guide's figures show them in perspective with mounting holes in the sides. Each carries an `empty` sentence.

poe-legend.note: The model plate prints the PoE count after "EX3200". The 24-port photographs show it ("8PoE" and "24PoE"); the 48-port plates are too small to read in the image held, so this model carries the count Table 3 gives, "48PoE", in the form of the 24-port plates. All ports are PoE ports, so the legend is chassis silkscreen. There is no -DC build of this model in Table 3.

port-lamps.note: Guide, Network Port LEDs in EX3200 Switches, Figure 10 and Tables 9 and 10: each 10/100/1000BASE-T port has two lamps, a Link/Activity lamp (green, blinking with activity, steady when linked) and a Status lamp whose meaning is chosen with the LCD Enter button (ADM, DPX, POE or SPD). The lamps are the jack housing's two corner windows (common/rj45-ganged-eth) and carry that component's default vocabulary; no source pairs the windows of the lower row, so the pairing is the component's.

port-numbering.note: The photograph prints the numbers in pairs above the top row of each column: 0 and 1 over the first column, 2 and 3 over the second, up to 46 and 47, the even number set higher and to the left, the odd lower and to the right (Figure 1 prints the same pairs). The even number belongs to the upper jack and the odd to the lower, so numbering runs down each column and then across. The numerals are drawn white at 2.2 mm type, estimated, and 2.2 mm either side of the column centre, because a mark that lands within 2 mm of the centre of the jack it names reads to lint as a slip at centring. The photograph is greyscale and shows no colour difference for the PoE ports. The guide's CLI interface names (ge-0/0/0 to ge-0/0/47) are not printed on the metal and are not modelled.

power.note: Guide Table 11: the 930 W supply of this model leaves a 740 W PoE budget for its 48 PoE ports, at up to 15.4 W each (up to 18.6 W with enhanced PoE from Junos OS 11.1). Table 14 gives 12 A for a switch with 48 PoE ports. The guide and the datasheet give no typical or maximum draw of the switch itself.

psu-seating.note: Guide Table 3 (the supply is "Power Supply (Minimum)": 930 W for this model) and Table 4 (PS 930W AC); the datasheet prints the code EX-PWR-930-AC, the same code the EX4200 uses, so that part is reused. This model's bay takes that supply only, the one at its minimum and the largest; Table 3 lists no DC build of this model.

rear.note: Guide Figure 3, rear seen from behind with x = 0 at the left of the drawing: the two earthing holes centred at (26.2, 14.0) and (45.8, 14.0) with the earth symbol below them at (35.2, 31.5); the temperature shutdown lamp centred at (48.0, 25.7); the management jack at 64.4 to 80.2 and the console jack at 88.3 to 104.1, each 27.9 to 41.1 mm down; the USB port at 121.7 to 133.7; the ESD point centred at (170.4, 11.4); the fan tray plate from 198.0 to 338.8 mm and 2.3 to 42.2 mm down; and the power supply slot from 339.0, 90.0 mm wide and 41.5 mm high from 2.5 mm down. The figure labels the supply "Power supply" and draws no second slot and no redundant power system port. The small round screws beside the earthing holes, the console jack and the USB port are not named by any callout and are not drawn.

rear-ground.note: Guide Table 33: for the EX3200 the earthing terminal is on the "Rear panel of the chassis", two 10-32 x 0.25 in screws with a Panduit LCC10-14BWL lug or equivalent. Figure 3 draws two holes 19.6 mm apart, which disagrees with the 5/8 in pitch of a two-hole lug; juniper/ex3400-ground-pair is reused, as the EX3300 does, set on the midpoint of the two holes.

rear-legends.note: Guide Figure 3 prints MGMT and CON above the two jacks, as horizontal words about 1.4 mm high. They are drawn so, with the earth symbol (a circle holding the earth mark) 12.5 mm across under the holes.

rear-temperature-lamp.note: Guide, Rear Panel of an EX3200 Switch: "Temperature shutdown LED", lit when the system shuts down because the chassis temperature has risen above the permitted level. No colour is stated.

sources.note: EX3200 Switch Hardware Guide, Juniper Networks, published 2020-12-15 (PDF in Juniper's EX Series documentation archive): Table 3 (models), Table 5 (chassis size and weight), Figures 1 and 2 (the 48-port and 24-port front panels), Figure 3 (rear panel), Figures 4 to 8 (LCD panel, uplink modules and chassis lamps), Figures 14 and 15 (fan tray and airflow), Figures 16 to 18 (supplies), Tables 11 to 15 (PoE budget and power) and Table 33 (earthing terminal). EX3200 Ethernet Switches datasheet (Juniper Networks, 12 pages, 1000216-013-EN, Nov 2011): Table 1 (models), specifications, per-model weights and noise, ordering information, and the four product photographs on page 4 (one image of 2175 x 654 px, greyscale). No quick-start figure and no studio photograph is used. Terms of use: the guide and datasheet are Juniper's, published by Juniper; none is copied into the library, only transcribed facts and new drawings. The guide's front and rear figures are vector line drawings with the top face in perspective and the datasheet photographs are perspective views from above, so every position is a measurement of a projection and is estimated, as the entries below say.

uplink-slot.note: Every EX3200 has one front-panel uplink module slot under a flip-up door held by screws; "Uplink modules are not part of the standard package and must be ordered separately", and installing one begins by removing "the blanking panel covering the empty uplink module slot". The slot is a bay that takes the cover here. The bay also takes the uplink modules the guide lists: EX-UM-4SFP (4 SFP ports), EX-UM-2X4SFP (2 SFP+ ports, or 4 SFP in 1-gigabit mode), its MACsec variant (EX-UM-2X4SFP-M, the number the EX4200 guide prints; this guide gives it none) and the XFP module (2 XFP ports; EX-UM-2XFP). The datasheet photographs show the slot with modules fitted, so they give the opening and not the cover.

references.title: EX3200 Switch Hardware Guide (Juniper Networks, published 2020-12-15)

bottom.empty: Not drawn by any source held: neither the guide nor the datasheet pictures the underside.

placements.description: Table 6 - ALM: red major alarm, amber minor alarm, unlit no alarm or halted (red at power-up until a network link is made)
Table 6 - SYS: green steady, Junos OS loaded; green blinking, booting; unlit, powered off or halted
Table 6 - MST: green, "meaningful only on EX4200 switches"

left.empty: Not drawn flat by any source held. The guide's perspective figures show the side panel with mounting holes; the front-mounting brackets are separate hardware.

placements.description: Rear panel - lit when the chassis temperature has risen above the permitted level and the system has shut down
Tables 7 and 8 - Link/Activity green blinking with activity, steady without, off when the port is not active; Status green steady when the administrative status is enabled, off when disabled

right.empty: Not drawn flat by any source held. The guide's perspective figures show the side panel with mounting holes; the front-mounting brackets are separate hardware.

top.empty: Not drawn flat by any source held. The guide's figures show the lid in perspective with mounting holes along the sides; nothing there can be measured.
